title: Agent platform with a tool gateway
description: An agent decides what to do, but every action it takes goes through one gateway that checks policy, asks a person for risky ones, and records everything.

detail.role: Give the agent a goal in plain language, such as refunding an order.
detail.why: The source of every task the agent takes on.

detail.role: Authenticates the caller and passes their identity to the agent.
detail.why: The agent acts for a named person, never for itself.

security.text: The agent receives a short-lived token scoped to what this person may do, not a shared service account.

cost.text: Each team has a cap on agent runs per day.

detail.role: Loops: asks the model what to do next, calls a tool, reads the result, and repeats until the goal is met or a step limit is hit.
detail.why: Keeps the loop, its limits and its state outside the model so they can be enforced.

cost.text: Each loop is another model call carrying the whole history, so a long task costs far more than its first step.

risks.text: A low limit abandons real tasks, a high one lets a confused agent run up the bill. It is set to 12 and reviewed monthly.

detail.role: Reads the goal and history and chooses the next tool call or the final answer.
detail.why: The model proposes; it never executes anything itself.

security.text: The model has no credentials. A wrong or manipulated choice still has to pass the gateway.

risks.text: Text read from a ticket or web page can try to steer the model. The gateway, not the prompt, is what limits the damage.

detail.role: Stores the plan, the steps taken and their results so a run can pause and resume.
detail.why: A task that waits for a human must survive a restart.

security.text: One person's run history is never loaded into another's context.

cost.text: Old steps are condensed so the prompt does not grow without limit.

detail.role: Receives every tool call, validates its arguments against the tool's schema, applies policy and forwards it with the user's delegated identity.
detail.why: Safety rules live in one place that no prompt can talk its way around.

security.text: The agent can only call tools registered for its task type. Anything else is refused.

risks.text: Tools accept calls only from the gateway's network identity, so the agent cannot reach them directly.

detail.role: Decides for each call whether to allow it, ask a person first, or deny it, using the tool, the arguments and who is asking.
detail.why: Rules are data that can be reviewed and tested, not behaviour hidden in a prompt.

security.text: A refund over a set amount, or any delete, needs a person. Read-only calls pass.

risks.text: Stricter rules mean more approvals and slower tasks. The threshold is tuned from how often approvers say no.

detail.role: Shows an approver the exact action and its arguments, and waits for yes or no.
detail.why: A person signs off on what is hard to undo.

risks.text: If nearly everything asks, approvers click through. Only actions that are costly or irreversible are routed here.

detail.role: Records who asked, what the model proposed, what policy decided and what the tool returned.
detail.why: When an agent does something odd, the record shows exactly why.

security.text: Entries cannot be edited, and the log sits in a separate account.

cost.text: Recent entries stay searchable and older ones move to cheap storage.

detail.role: The real systems the agent acts on.
detail.why: They keep their own permissions and validation, so a gateway mistake is not the only defence.

security.text: The gateway exchanges the user's identity for a token valid for one tool and a few minutes.

links.label: Goal
links.detail: A task is submitted and progress and the result come back on the same connection.

links.label: Run with identity
links.detail: The gateway starts a run and hands over the caller's delegated token.

links.label: Next step?
links.detail: The agent sends the goal, the history and the tool list, and gets back a tool call or an answer.

links.label: Save state
links.detail: After every step the run is written, so it can resume after a pause or a crash.

links.label: Tool call
links.detail: The agent sends the model's proposed call. It never talks to a tool directly.

links.label: Check
links.detail: The gateway asks for a decision on this tool, these arguments and this caller.

links.label: Forwarded call
links.detail: An allowed call is forwarded with a narrow, short-lived token, and the result returns.

links.label: Ask a person
links.detail: When policy says to ask, the call waits and an approver is notified. The run pauses without holding a worker.

links.label: Decision record
links.detail: Every decision, allowed or refused, is written with the call that caused it.

trace.label: A staff member asks the agent to refund an order
The gateway issues a token scoped to that person
The goal and plan are saved
The agent asks the model what to do first
The model proposes calling the refund tool
The agent sends that call to the gateway
The gateway checks the call against the tool's schema
Policy allows it, since the amount is under the limit
The refund runs in the payments system
